definition: Neural architecture search (NAS) is a technique for automating the design of artificial neural networks (ANN), a widely used model in the field of machine learning.
details: NAS has been used to design networks that are on par with or outperform hand-designed architectures. Methods for NAS can be categorized according to the search space, search strategy and performance estimation strategy used: The search space defines the type(s) of ANN that can be designed and optimized. The search strategy defines the approach used to explore the search space. The performance estimation strategy evaluates the performance of a possible ANN from its design (without constructing and training it). NAS is closely related to hyperparameter optimization and meta-learning and is a subfield of automated machine learning (AutoML).

explainer.lead: Neural architecture search automates the design of artificial neural networks, a widely used machine learning model. It has produced networks on par with or better than hand-designed architectures.

tiers.eli5: Instead of a person guessing the best shape for a model, a program tries many shapes and keeps the best one.
tiers.practitioner: Methods are categorized by search space (which networks can be designed), search strategy (how the space is explored) and performance estimation strategy (how a design is judged without full construction). A pitfall is that performance estimation must stand in for training, so a weak estimator misleads the search.
tiers.paperLevel: A technique for automating ANN design, categorized by search space, search strategy and performance estimation strategy; the estimation strategy evaluates a possible ANN from its design without constructing it.

explainer.example: A search strategy explores a defined space of architectures, and a performance estimation strategy scores each design from its description before committing to training.
